author: David Reed
summary: Closes the silent-fallback pattern iter-14 fixed one instance of. chg-19: GuidelineRetriever.query() returns a structured RetrievalOutcome (text, mode, degraded, reason) instead of a bare str, making a RAGPipeline failure visible to the caller instead of only a log line. chg-20: the submit route always audits a degraded retrieval and, behind a warn-by-default flag, can force human review instead of letting the DecisionAgent reason over unverified fallback context.

changes.description: GuidelineRetriever.query() returns RetrievalOutcome(text, mode, degraded, reason) instead of a bare str. mode is 'pipeline' (intended path), 'direct_fallback' (pipeline unavailable/raised, fallback found something), or 'empty' (fallback found nothing in either collection). reason is the exception TYPE name only, never the raw message.
changes.failure_pattern: GuidelineRetriever.query() catches any exception from the real RAGPipeline, logs at error level, and silently falls back to the legacy direct-ChromaDB path, returning a plausible-looking str either way. The caller (the submit route, the DecisionAgent's prompt context) cannot distinguish governed retrieval from degraded retrieval. vector_store.py has the highest density of broad `except Exception` in the codebase (5 in 353 lines); this is the constructor/query pair that feeds a clinical decision.
changes.root_cause: The return type of query() was always `str`, so there was no channel for the method to say 'I degraded' short of a log line at error level — which nothing downstream reads. iter-14 (chg-17) fixed one concrete instance of this pattern (a bad import that latched the fallback permanently) but did not change the return type, so any future pipeline failure — a ChromaDB connection error, an embedding-function exception, a malformed query — reproduces the same invisible degradation.

evidence.note: "a silent fallback plus an unimportable module is indistinguishable from a working system" — the general claim this change acts on, not just the specific import bug iter-14 fixed.
Before this change there was no way to express or test 'the pipeline never ran and the fallback found nothing' as a distinct, non-crashing outcome — it looked identical to a healthy empty result.
Regression guard: a synthetic PHI-like exception message is asserted absent from RetrievalOutcome.reason — only the exception's type name crosses the boundary that chg-20 writes into an audit record.

predicted_fixes: A RAGPipeline failure (ChromaDB error, embedding-function exception, any future exception in the retrieval path) is now distinguishable from a healthy retrieval by mode/degraded on the return value, not just a log line.

An unseeded or genuinely empty retrieval (mode='empty') is distinguishable from a real fallback that found something (mode='direct_fallback'), so an operator reading audit records can tell 'degraded but real context' from 'the agent decided on nothing'.
Every existing call site of query() (7 files found by repo-wide grep) is updated in the same change, per repo lesson P-005 on contract changes.
risk_cases: Any call site not caught by the grep for '.query(' would silently break (AttributeError on .text) rather than degrade gracefully — mitigated by grepping the whole repo, not just files already open.

A test double that still returns a bare str instead of a RetrievalOutcome would raise inside the route rather than being caught by the existing except Exception -> 500 handler in a semantically odd way — verified none remain by running the full non-clinical suite.
changes.why_this_component: The defect is in the retrieval tool's return contract, not in how any agent reasons over the text it receives — the agent-visible prompt content is unchanged in shape (still `.text`), only the caller's ability to detect degradation changed.
changes.rollback_plan: Revert all files in this change together (one commit per file, three commits: vector_store.py, the authorizations.py call-site fix, and the test call-site updates). A partial revert of just vector_store.py breaks every call site immediately (AttributeError on .text); revert the full set or not at all.

changes.description: The submit route audits every degraded RetrievalOutcome (action='rag.degraded') before proceeding, and a new settings.rag_degraded_escalates flag (default False) can force the case to human review (IN_REVIEW/HUMAN, EscalationReason.RAG_DEGRADED) instead of letting the DecisionAgent reason over unverified fallback context.
changes.failure_pattern: Even after chg-19 makes degradation visible in the return value, nothing acted on it: a degraded RetrievalOutcome could still flow straight into the DecisionAgent's prompt with no audit trail and no escalation path, leaving the same clinical-visibility gap one layer up the call stack.
changes.root_cause: Visibility (chg-19) and policy (chg-20) are different constraint levels — the return-type contract belongs in the tool implementation, but 'what happens when it's degraded' is a governance/escalation decision that belongs at the route, alongside the existing ScopeViolation and evidence-grounding short-circuits.

evidence.note: Direct precedent for the warn-then-enforce rollout shape reused here: land audited-but-non-blocking, promote once production degradation rates are known.

Drives the real submit_authorization handler with a degraded RetrievalOutcome and rag_degraded_escalates=True; asserts IN_REVIEW/HUMAN, the escalation audit record, and that the orchestrator never runs.

predicted_fixes: Every RAG degradation in production now leaves an audit record (action='rag.degraded') regardless of the escalation flag, closing the 'no trace of what context the agent actually saw' gap.
Operators can flip rag_degraded_escalates to True once they have data on how often degradation fires, without another code change.
risk_cases: If degradation fires far more often than expected (e.g. a flaky embedding function), warn mode means many decisions proceed on fallback context before anyone notices — mitigated by the audit record being written every time, so the rate is observable without needing enforce mode on.

Flipping rag_degraded_escalates to True without first observing production rates could flood the human review queue, per the same risk the P-4 scope guard rollout was designed against — this is why the default stays False here.
changes.why_this_component: This is a new deterministic pre-agent short-circuit in the 7-branch escalation tree's spirit (though it lives in the route rather than the orchestrator, matching where the RAG query itself happens, before DecisionContext is built) — the same constraint level as SCOPE_VIOLATION, not a tool or prompt change.
changes.rollback_plan: Revert all three files together (settings.py, enums.py, authorizations.py each landed as their own commit). Reverting only settings.py would leave a dangling EscalationReason.RAG_DEGRADED reference in authorizations.py; revert the full set.
